justification: Diagnosis-driven fixes from the first full (uncut) live brief. (1) SHADOW now succeeds (the earlier 65s budget fix landed) but rendered as a bare '6 fields'; added a ShadowDisplay component that renders the real overshadowing summary (modelled height + source, ADG 3-hour solar-access compliance badge, worst-case shadow length + neighbour overlap, temporal caveat). (2) TERRAIN failed with a generic 'imagery or model source unavailable' that hid the cause; the brief now passes through the REAL terrain_df.reason and the satellite empty-state surfaces it (capped) so the actual error (DEM/whitebox) is diagnosable on the next run. (3) PRE-DA's confirmed 'No module named rapidfuzz' — rapidfuzz is imported by services/pre_da_history.py but was missing from services/requirements.txt (the file the prod Docker image installs, NOT the root requirements.txt); added it. NOTE: pre-DA also needs torch (Tessera/Clay embeddings) which services/requirements.txt deliberately excludes as too large for Railway — so pre-DA ultimately needs decoupling to a GPU worker like granny-flat; rapidfuzz is a correct omission fix regardless.

pre_impl.existing_data: Shadow is a DataField[Optional[ShadowResult]] inside Neighbourhood; ShadowResult has height_m/height_source/adg_compliant/scenarios/worst_case_scenario/temporal_caveat. terrain_df.reason already captures the real _safe_call exception. services/requirements.txt (49 lines) is what Dockerfile.python installs.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed the root requirements.txt governed the prod image; in fact Dockerfile.python installs services/requirements.txt, which omits rapidfuzz (and deliberately torch).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reused the existing nested-render pattern (like HeritageList/OverlayList) for shadow; reused the DataField.reason already produced by _safe_call for terrain; appended one dependency.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Terrain/flood/shadow upstream failures now surface their real reason (capped) instead of a generic line; a genuine success renders the data.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Frontend (shadow render + reason surfacing) + backend (terrain reason passthrough + one requirement). tsc passes; 159 brief tests pass.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: shadow showed '6 fields'; terrain showed a generic 'unavailable' with no cause; pre-DA failed on a missing package. After: shadow shows the overshadowing summary; terrain shows its real error; pre-DA's rapidfuzz blocker is removed (torch decoupling still needed for the embeddings).

functions.name: ShadowDisplay
functions.input: a ShadowResult object with height, ADG compliance, scenarios and worst-case
functions.output: a readable overshadowing summary with a solar-access compliance badge and the worst-case shadow length and neighbour overlap
functions.if_none: a null shadow value hits the not_available branch and shows the unavailable message instead

functions.name: describeUnavailable
functions.input: a satellite layer's reason, section and satelliteRan flag
functions.output: for a ran-but-failed satellite layer, the generic message now appends the real reason (capped at 180 chars) when it is not a 'not requested' case
functions.if_none: a not-requested layer still shows the tick-the-box message

values: N/A - shadow geometry and a dependency, not regulatory values.

break_it.scenario: Shadow result is present but has no scenarios array
break_it.what_happens: the worst-case line would be skipped and only height/ADG show
break_it.how: each block is guarded by a null/empty check; an empty scenarios array simply omits the worst-case line

break_it.scenario: A satellite reason contains a very long Python traceback
break_it.what_happens: an unwieldy string could show in the card
break_it.repro: terrain raises with a long message
break_it.how: the reason is capped at 180 chars and framed in parentheses; this is a dev/demo tool where the visible reason is what enables diagnosis

break_it.scenario: rapidfuzz still missing after deploy because the image build cache is stale
break_it.what_happens: pre-DA would still fail on rapidfuzz
break_it.repro: Railway reuses the cached pip layer
break_it.how: adding it to services/requirements.txt changes the file content, invalidating the pip layer cache; if Railway still serves a stale image, a clean rebuild resolves it

break_it.scenario: Adding rapidfuzz makes pre-DA appear fixed but it still fails on torch
break_it.what_happens: pre-DA shows a torch error instead of rapidfuzz
break_it.how: the surfaced real reason will now show the torch/geotessera error, confirming pre-DA needs decoupling to a GPU worker — documented in services/requirements.txt
